    29	
    30	/-- Euclidean space `ℝ^d`. -/
    31	abbrev Rd (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
    32	
    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤
    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    39	  ν.map (fun x => -x) = ν
    40	
    41	/-- Positive-definiteness of `Γ` as a tempered distribution:
    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re
    48	
    49	/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention
    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:
    51	`∫ φ dΓ = ∫ (∫ φ(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx) μ(dξ)` for every Schwartz `φ`. -/
    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    53	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ
    56	
    57	/-- Hypothesis `H:homog`. Let `d ∈ {1,2,3}` and `0 < α₀ < 1`. The spatial
    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)
    81	
    82	/-- The numerical part of `H:homog`, in the form used by `DriverParameters`
    83	(with `a = α₀`). -/
    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    85	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    86	    DriverParameters.Homog d alpha alpha0 :=
    87	  ⟨h.dim, h.alpha0_pos, h.alpha0_lt_one, by linarith [h.threshold], h.alpha_range⟩
    88	
    89	/-- `E:kappa` with the manuscript's hypothesis: under `H:homog`,
    90	`κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α) ∈ (1, 2)`. -/
    91	theorem kappa_mem_Ioo_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    92	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    93	    KappaRange.kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 :=
    94	  KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo d alpha alpha0 h.dim h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one
    95	    h.threshold h.alpha_range
    96	
    97	/-- `E:driver-parameters` with the manuscript's hypothesis (the section
    98	retains `H:homog` and sets `a = α₀`): its strict intervals are nonempty. -/
    99	theorem parameters_nonempty_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   100	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
   101	    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
   102	      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - alpha0 / 2) ((3 - alpha0 - alpha) / 2)) :=
   103	  DriverParameters.parameters_nonempty d alpha alpha0 (homog_params h)
   104	
   105	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.HomogHypothesis

     7	`notes/integrated_raw_block_lower.tex` (TeX lines 227--330 at revision

    10	Class: inputs-supplied.  The lemma uses only the outputs of Section
    11	`S:compact-mean-family` (`notes/integrated_compact_mean_family.tex`) for the

    13	fields are stated as the TeX states them (TeX lines and labels in each field's
    14	doc comment):
    15	* `P_σ(t)` bounded operators on a real normed space `F` (the physical flow of
    16	  `S:compact-mean-family`, line 17; `E:compact-F-block`);
    17	* vectors `e_σ`, functionals `ℓ_σ`, rank-one projections `Π_σ = e_σ ℓ_σ` and
    18	  `Q_σ = I - Π_σ` (`E:compact-F-projection`, lines 270--272);
    19	* rates `λ_σ > 0` (`E:compact-rate-gap` gives `√ε ≤ λ_σ`, line 51; only
    20	  positivity is kept);
    21	* `ℓ_σ(e_σ) = 1`, `P_σ(t)Π_σ = Π_σP_σ(t) = e^{λ_σ t}Π_σ`

    24	  `0 < η < d_0` (`E:compact-normalized-complement`, lines 344--348), with

    28	  275--276); continuity and uniform boundedness of `Π_σ`, and uniform
    29	  boundedness of `e_σ, ℓ_σ`, are DERIVED here (compactness), not assumed;
    30	* the margins `inf_I ℓ_σ(e_0) > 0`, `inf_I O_φ(e_σ) > 0`
    31	  (`E:compact-positive-margins`, lines 283--286), with the data `e_0` and the

    34	The structure is no stronger than Propositions `P:compact-F-projection` and
    35	`P:compact-F-complement` (with `P:compact-ground-family` for `λ_σ > 0`,
    36	`d_0 > 0`): every field is one of their displayed conclusions, or a weakening
    37	of one.  It does not encode `P_σ` as a semigroup, the spectral structure, or

    39	
    40	Side conditions made explicit:
    41	* the TeX fixes `E_0 = ‖e_0‖ = 1`; here `‖e_0‖` is arbitrary (the constants are

    61	
    62	@[expose] public section
    63

    68	open Set Filter Topology
    69	
    70	namespace StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.IndexedCone
    71	
    72	/-- The family-parameter interval `I = [0,1]` of `S:compact-mean-family`
    73	(TeX `integrated_compact_mean_family.tex`, line 4). -/
    74	def paramI : Set ℝ := Icc 0 1
    75	
    76	/-- `I = [0,1]` is compact (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
    77	theorem isCompact_paramI : IsCompact paramI := isCompact_Icc
    78	
    79	/-- The C16 outputs used by `L:raw-block-indexed-cone`, supplied as one
    80	hypothesis structure (inputs-supplied; see the module doc).  `P σ t` is the
    81	flow `P_σ(t)`, `e σ` and `ell σ` are `e_σ` and `ℓ_σ`, `lam σ` is `λ_σ`, `e0`
    82	is the data `e_0` and `obs` is the bounded observable `O_φ`. -/
    83	structure GroundFamily (F : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] where
    84	  /-- The bounded flows `P_σ(t)` on `F` (`E:compact-F-block`). -/
    85	  P : ℝ → ℝ → F →L[ℝ] F
    86	  /-- The growing vectors `e_σ` (`E:compact-F-projection`). -/
    87	  e : ℝ → F
    88	  /-- The growing duals `ℓ_σ` (`E:compact-F-projection`). -/
    89	  ell : ℝ → F →L[ℝ] ℝ
    90	  /-- The rates `λ_σ = √(-E_1(σ))` (`P:compact-ground-family`). -/
    91	  lam : ℝ → ℝ
    92	  /-- The data `e_0` (`S:actual-raw-block-lower`, line 15). -/
    93	  e0 : F
    94	  /-- The bounded observable `O_φ` (`S:actual-raw-block-lower`, line 15). -/
    95	  obs : F →L[ℝ] ℝ
    96	  /-- The uniform rate gap `d_0` (`E:compact-rate-gap`). -/
    97	  d0 : ℝ
    98	  /-- `λ_σ ≥ √ε > 0` on `I` (`E:compact-rate-gap`; positivity only). -/
    99	  lam_pos : ∀ σ ∈ paramI, 0 < lam σ
   100	  /-- `ℓ_σ(e_σ) = 1` (`E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   101	  ell_e : ∀ σ ∈ paramI, ell σ (e σ) = 1
   102	  /-- `P_σ(t)Π_σ = e^{λ_σ t}Π_σ` (`E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   103	  P_Pi : ∀ σ ∈ paramI, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
   104	    (P σ t).comp ((ell σ).smulRight (e σ)) =
   105	      Real.exp (lam σ * t) • (ell σ).smulRight (e σ)
   106	  /-- `Π_σP_σ(t) = e^{λ_σ t}Π_σ` (`E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   107	  Pi_P : ∀ σ ∈ paramI, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
   108	    ((ell σ).smulRight (e σ)).comp (P σ t) =
   109	      Real.exp (lam σ * t) • (ell σ).smulRight (e σ)
   110	  /-- `d_0 > 0` (`E:compact-rate-gap`). -/
   111	  d0_pos : 0 < d0
   112	  /-- `‖e^{-λ_σ t}P_σ(t)Q_σ‖ ≤ C_η e^{-ηt}` uniformly over `σ ∈ I`, `t ≥ 0`,
   113	  for every `0 < η < d_0` (`E:compact-normalized-complement`). -/
   114	  normalized_complement : ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → η < d0 → ∃ C : ℝ,
   115	    ∀ σ ∈ paramI, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
   116	      ‖Real.exp (-(lam σ * t)) •
   117	          (P σ t).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ F - (ell σ).smulRight (e σ))‖
   118	        ≤ C * Real.exp (-(η * t))
   119	  /-- Norm continuity of `σ ↦ e_σ` on `I` (`P:compact-F-projection`). -/
   120	  e_cont : ContinuousOn e paramI
   121	  /-- Norm continuity of `σ ↦ ℓ_σ` on `I` (`P:compact-F-projection`). -/
   122	  ell_cont : ContinuousOn ell paramI
   123	  /-- `inf_I ℓ_σ(e_0) > 0` (`E:compact-positive-margins`). -/
   124	  margin_ell : 0 < ⨅ σ : paramI, ell σ e0
   125	  /-- `inf_I O_φ(e_σ) > 0` (`E:compact-positive-margins`). -/
   126	  margin_obs : 0 < ⨅ σ : paramI, obs (e σ)
   127	
   128	namespace GroundFamily
   129	
   130	variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (G : GroundFamily F)
   131	
   132	/-- The rank-one projection `Π_σ = e_σ ℓ_σ` (`E:compact-F-projection`). -/
   133	def Pi (σ : ℝ) : F →L[ℝ] F := (G.ell σ).smulRight (G.e σ)
   134	
   135	/-- The complementary projection `Q_σ = I - Π_σ` (`E:compact-F-projection`). -/
   136	def Q (σ : ℝ) : F →L[ℝ] F := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ F - G.Pi σ
   137	
   138	/-- The margin `a_* = inf_I ℓ_σ(e_0)` (TeX line 254). -/
   139	def aStar : ℝ := ⨅ σ : paramI, G.ell σ G.e0
   140	
   141	/-- The margin `j_* = inf_I O_φ(e_σ)` (TeX line 254). -/
   142	def jStar : ℝ := ⨅ σ : paramI, G.obs (G.e σ)
   143	
   144	/-- `Π_σ x = ℓ_σ(x) e_σ` (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   145	theorem Pi_apply (σ : ℝ) (x : F) : G.Pi σ x = G.ell σ x • G.e σ := rfl
   146	
   147	/-- `Q_σ x = x - ℓ_σ(x) e_σ` (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   148	theorem Q_apply (σ : ℝ) (x : F) : G.Q σ x = x - G.ell σ x • G.e σ := rfl
   149	
   150	/-- `ℓ_σ P_σ(t) = e^{λ_σ t} ℓ_σ` (from `E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   151	theorem ell_P {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ∈ paramI) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) (x : F) :
   152	    G.ell σ (G.P σ t x) = Real.exp (G.lam σ * t) * G.ell σ x := by
   153	  have h := congrArg (fun T : F →L[ℝ] F => G.ell σ (T x)) (G.Pi_P σ hσ t ht)
   154	  simpa [ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_apply, G.ell_e σ hσ] using h
   155	
   156	/-- `P_σ(t)e_σ = e^{λ_σ t}e_σ` (from `E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   157	theorem P_e {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ∈ paramI) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
   158	    G.P σ t (G.e σ) = Real.exp (G.lam σ * t) • G.e σ := by
   159	  have h := congrArg (fun T : F →L[ℝ] F => T (G.e σ)) (G.P_Pi σ hσ t ht)
   160	  simpa [ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_apply, G.ell_e σ hσ] using h
   161	
   162	/-- `ℓ_σ Q_σ = 0` (TeX line 280, `ℓ_s(r) = 0`). -/
   163	theorem ell_Q {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ∈ paramI) (x : F) : G.ell σ (G.Q σ x) = 0 := by
   164	  simp [Q_apply, G.ell_e σ hσ]
   165	
   166	/-- `Q_σ² = Q_σ` (TeX line 281, `r = Q_s z`). -/
   167	theorem Q_Q {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ∈ paramI) (x : F) : G.Q σ (G.Q σ x) = G.Q σ x := by

1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels refer to the manuscript
     6	revision 3920258 and are written exactly as in its LaTeX source (for
     7	example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written and reviewed
     8	at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9 and ba01d98. The later revisions
     9	changed only prose, titles, the literature review, layout and figures:
    10	every cited label exists in all four, and the mathematical expressions of
    11	each cited statement and its proof are the same up to whitespace and braces
    12	(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    13	
    14	## Scope
    15	
    16	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    17	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    18	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`; `Audit/<module>/` prints the
    19	  elaborated types.
    20	- The rows cover every public theorem (470) and 87 definitions whose
    21	  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other
    22	  49 public definitions (for example
    23	  `kappa`, `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`) only name quantities used in those
    24	  statements and have no rows of their own; read their bodies in the Lean
    25	  source or in `Audit/`.
    26	- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
    27	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    28	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
    29	  inner-product and finite-word facts.
    30	- The nineteen `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules (sections marked
    31	  "whole result" below; four of them are the wave-kernel and
    32	  time-fractional foundation of `ClockCopy`) model `H:homog` and formalize
    33	  the conclusions of fifteen
    34	  labelled results in full. Eleven need no supplied input:
    35	  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own
    36	  hypotheses. `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are
    37	  proved under weaker hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no
    38	  `delta < 1`) and also stated exactly as the manuscript does by the
    39	  wrappers `gram_scalar_algebra_paper` and `rayleigh_tail_paper`; the
    40	  Rayleigh lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is
    41	  not formalized. `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters` are proved from the
    42	  numerical part of `H:homog` (a generalization) and also restated under
    43	  the full hypothesis `H:homog`, which `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`
    44	  models clause by clause (covariance measure, spectral measure, evenness,
    45	  temperedness, positive-definiteness, scaling, parameter ranges).
    46	  `L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` and `L:temporal-equilibrium` are stated with
    47	  the manuscript's own hypotheses (`gamma_beta_paper`,
    48	  `temporal_equilibrium_paper`). The finite slice of `S:compact-gaussian`,
    49	  `L:gaussian-trace-bounds`, `P:finite-gaussian-matrix` and
    50	  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`, is stated with the manuscript's
    51	  hypotheses (independent standard Gaussians on an arbitrary probability
    52	  space) on top of a finite Gaussian integration-by-parts foundation
    53	  (`GaussianIBP`). `L:variational-control-dilation` is
    54	  stated with the section's hypotheses (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a =
    55	  alpha0`) by `variational_control_dilation_paper`, for the cost in its
    56	  integral form and the rate defined by the real Rayleigh supremum
    57	  `E:variational-real-rayleigh` (over a weak-gradient `H^1(R^d)` built in
    58	  `WeakSobolev`, since Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces); the identifications
    59	  with `E W(Psi)^2` and `sqrt(-E_s)` are not formalized. Four further results are formalized with
    60	  every conclusion proved but with analytic inputs supplied as named
    61	  hypotheses: `P:radius-mean-anchor` (the moment bound of
    62	  `C:radius-covariance-residuals`, and measurability of the Holder norm of
    63	  the stopped paths) and `L:masked-trig-products` (membership in the
    64	  temporal completion, `L:masked-time-completion`, and the modulation
    65	  bound `L:masked-temporal-modulation`) and `L:raw-block-indexed-cone`
    66	  (the ground family of `S:compact-mean-family`, one hypothesis structure)
    67	  and `P:clock-copy-obstruction` (the homogeneity of the spectral measure,
    68	  which the TeX derives in the proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`; the
    69	  finiteness part of that lemma is also formalized);
    70	  their abstractions are explained
    71	  in their sections. Side conditions the TeX leaves implicit (a probability
    72	  measure, integrability, measurability) are explicit hypotheses, and
    73	  integrability is part of each integral conclusion.
    74	- The SPDE itself, stochastic integrals, Gaussian measures (beyond finitely
    75	  many independent standard Gaussians, `GaussianIBP`), Fourier and
    76	  spectral analysis, operator theory and all limits in time or in a
    77	  regularization are outside Lean. Where a Lean statement needs an analytic
    78	  fact about the model, that fact enters as an explicit hypothesis of the
    79	  theorem (a "supplied hypothesis" below). Lean checks the deduction from
    80	  those hypotheses, not the hypotheses themselves.
    81	- A successful `lake build` is not a verification receipt for the
    82	  manuscript. It shows that the stated Lean theorems are proved from their
    83	  hypotheses; whether a statement matches the manuscript step it is listed
    84	  against is a separate, human judgment recorded in this ledger.
    85	- Three further modules developed alongside these (normalized Gaussian
    86	  coordinates, vector Gaussian projection, and colored vector words) are
    87	  withheld from this package because they depend on a library that is not
    88	  yet public.
    89	- "no direct label" means the declaration checks a computation from the
    90	  development of the manuscript that does not appear as, or inside, a
    91	  labeled statement of the revision cited above. Such rows make no claim
    92	  about the manuscript.

   446	`L:raw-block-indexed-cone`, where a cone around a slowly moving dominant

   152	\section{Model and standing assumptions}\label{S:model}
   153	
   154	We study the hyperbolic Anderson model
   155	\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(1.1)}
   156	\begin{equation}\label{E:HAM}
   157	  \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}(t,x)=\Delta u(t,x)+\W(t,x)u(t,x),
   158	  \qquad u(0,x)=1,\quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0,x)=0,
   159	\end{equation}
   160	for $(t,x) \in \R_+\times\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$, interpreted in the
   161	Stratonovich sense (limit of classical wave equations driven by smoothed noises
   162	$\W_{\epsilon,\delta}$). The noise is centered Gaussian with
   163	\begin{equation}\label{E:cov}
   164	  \operatorname{Cov}\big(\W(s,x),\W(t,y)\big)=|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}\gamma(x-y),
   165	  \qquad 0<\alpha_0<1,
   166	\end{equation}
   167	where $\gamma \ge 0$ is nonnegative definite with spectral measure $\mu$.
   168	
   169	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   170	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   171	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   172	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   173	  convention
   174	  \[
   175	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   176	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
   177	  \]
   178	  The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
   179	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   180	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   181	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   182	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   183	  \end{equation}
   184	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   185	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   186	\end{hypothesis}
   187	
   188	Throughout we write
   189	\begin{equation}\label{E:kappa}
   190	  \kappa:=\frac{4-\alpha-\alpha_0}{3-\alpha}\in(1,2).
   191	\end{equation}
   192	
   193	\paragraph{Contribution of the present work.}
   194	We address the second moment of the original Stratonovich solution with
   195	fractional temporal covariance throughout Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. The
   196	independent upper bound reaches the scale $t^\kappa$, rather than only the
   197	coarse quadratic exponential scale in the source. The main identification gives
   198	an intrinsic variational expression for the limiting constant over all
   199	nonnegative smooth compact spacetime controls, without a separability
   200	restriction. It retains the covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and a
   201	Gaussian cost equal to one half of the variance, and includes the zero
   202	covariance case. The upper and lower comparisons refer to the same canonical
   203	solution. The occupation and spatial-energy estimates then give bounds on this
   204	constant; evaluating the white spatial energy is not a numerical evaluation of
   205	the full moment supremum. The earlier results discussed below concern different
   206	stochastic interpretations or temporal covariances and do not supply this
   207	identification by substitution.

    33	\begin{proposition}[Ground states and a uniform rate gap]
    34	  \label{P:compact-ground-family}
    35	  The common form domain of $H_\sigma$ is $H^1$ with form $q_\sigma(u) =
    36	  \|\nabla u\|_2^2-\int V_\sigma|u|^2$. Its bottom $E_1(\sigma)$ is a simple
    37	  eigenvalue with a unique real positive-a.e. normalized ground state
    38	  $p_\sigma$. Let $E_2(\sigma)$ be the second max--min level, set to zero when
    39	  there is no second negative eigenvalue. Then
    40	  \begin{align}
    41	    -M&\le E_1(\sigma)\le-\varepsilon,\qquad
    42	    E_1(\sigma)<E_2(\sigma)\le0,\label{E:compact-energy-levels}\\
    43	    |E_j(\sigma)-E_j(\tau)|
    44	    &\le\|V_\sigma-V_\tau\|_\infty,\qquad j=1,2.
    45	    \label{E:compact-level-continuity}
    46	  \end{align}
    47	  The map $\sigma\mapsto p_\sigma$ is continuous into $H^2$ and bounded there.
    48	  With $\lambda_\sigma = \sqrt{-E_1(\sigma)}$ and $\mu_\sigma =
    49	  \sqrt{-E_2(\sigma)}$,
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-rate-gap}
    51	    \sqrt\varepsilon\le\lambda_\sigma\le\sqrt M,\qquad
    52	    d_0:=\inf_I(\lambda_\sigma-\mu_\sigma)>0.
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{proposition}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  The imported Theorem~10.2 applies to $-V_\sigma$, which is real, compactly
    58	  supported and in $L^2$ for $d \le 3$. It gives the stated self-adjoint
    59	  operator on $H^2$ and essential threshold zero. Write $c = 1+M$ and $A_\sigma
    60	  = H_\sigma+c \ge 1$. On $H^2$, integration by parts and the spectral theorem
    61	  give
    62	  \[
    63	    \|A_\sigma^{1/2}u\|_2^2
    64	    =q_\sigma(u)+c\|u\|_2^2,\qquad
    65	    \|u\|_{H^1}^2\le\|A_\sigma^{1/2}u\|_2^2
    66	    \le c\|u\|_{H^1}^2.
    67	  \]
    68	  Spectral cutoffs $1_{[1,n]}(A_\sigma)u$ show that $H^2$ is a core for the
    69	  half-power form norm. Fourier cutoffs show it is dense in $H^1$. The two
    70	  equivalent completions are therefore $D(A_\sigma^{1/2})$ and $H^1$. Both norms
    71	  dominate $L^2$ and give the same $L^2$ limit, so these are equal as subspaces,
    72	  with the displayed form. This verifies the form domain used below.
    73	
    74	  The form lower bound and~\eqref{E:compact-common-trial} give $-M \le E_1 \le
    75	  -\varepsilon$ by the imported form max--min principle. The bottom belongs to
    76	  the spectrum and lies below the essential threshold, so it is an isolated
    77	  eigenvalue of finite multiplicity. Only now apply the imported Theorem~10.13:
    78	  it is simple with a positive ground state. Conjugation preserves the real
    79	  operator; positivity and unit $L^2$ norm fix its real representative.
    80	
    81	  Simplicity, isolation and threshold zero give $E_1 < E_2 \le 0$. For every
    82	  common unit form test, $|q_\sigma(u)-q_\tau(u)| \le
    83	  \|V_\sigma-V_\tau\|_\infty$. Taking the same infima over orthogonal

    85	  \eqref{E:compact-level-continuity}, including passage of $E_2$ to the

    87	  \[
    88	    \lambda_\sigma-\mu_\sigma
    89	    =\frac{E_2(\sigma)-E_1(\sigma)}
    90	    {\lambda_\sigma+\mu_\sigma}
    91	    \ge\frac{\Delta_*}{2\sqrt M}>0.
    92	  \]
    93	  Here $M \ge \varepsilon > 0$, and no division by $\mu_\sigma$ occurs.
    94	
    95	  Put $d_V = \|V_\sigma-V_\tau\|_\infty$ and decompose $p_\tau = a p_\sigma+r$,

    99	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-ground-continuity}

   114	\begin{lemma}[Uniform fractional phase norms]\label{L:compact-fractional-phase}

   156	  scalar multiple of $A_\sigma^{-1/2}z$ attains it. Completion
   157	  and~\eqref{E:compact-quarter-power} identify this negative space with
   158	  $H^{-1/2}$, uniformly in $\sigma$. Adding the squared norms proves the claim.
   159	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:compact-fractional-phase}.
   160	\end{proof}

   162	\begin{proposition}[The complementary wave on $E$]\label{P:compact-E-wave}
   163	  Put
   164	  \[
   165	    e_\sigma^E=(p_\sigma,\lambda_\sigma p_\sigma),\qquad
   166	    \ell_\sigma^E(u,z)
   167	    =\frac{\langle p_\sigma,u\rangle+
   168	    \langle p_\sigma,z\rangle/\lambda_\sigma}{2},
   169	    \qquad \Pi_\sigma^E=e_\sigma^E\ell_\sigma^E.
   170	  \]
   171	  These are bounded real objects, continuous in their respective norms, with
   172	  $\ell_\sigma^E(e_\sigma^E) = 1$, and
   173	  \begin{align}
   174	    P_\sigma^E(t)e_\sigma^E
   175	    &=e^{\lambda_\sigma t}e_\sigma^E,\qquad
   176	    \ell_\sigma^EP_\sigma^E(t)
   177	    =e^{\lambda_\sigma t}\ell_\sigma^E,\label{E:compact-E-eigen}\\
   178	    \|P_\sigma^E(t)(I-\Pi_\sigma^E)\|_{\mathcal{B}(E)}
   179	    &\le C(1+t)e^{\mu_\sigma t},\qquad t\ge0.
   180	    \label{E:compact-E-complement}
   181	  \end{align}
   182	  The constant is uniform over $\sigma \in I$.
   183	\end{proposition}
   184	
   185	\begin{proof}
   186	  Define real spectral functions $C_t(h),S_t(h)$ by $\cos(t\sqrt h),\sin(t\sqrt
   187	  h)/\sqrt h$ for $h > 0$, by $1,t$ at zero, and by
   188	  $\cosh(t\sqrt{-h}),\sinh(t\sqrt{-h})/\sqrt{-h}$ for $h < 0$. The spectral wave
   189	  matrix is
   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-spectral-wave}
   191	    \begin{pmatrix}
   192	      C_t(H_\sigma)&S_t(H_\sigma)\\
   193	      -H_\sigma S_t(H_\sigma)&C_t(H_\sigma)
   194	    \end{pmatrix}.
   195	  \end{equation}
   196	  Real potentials, their resolvents and spectral resolutions commute with
   197	  conjugation. All these real functions and positive $A_\sigma$ powers preserve
   198	  the real phases.
   199	
   200	  The spatial projection $Q_\sigma^{\mathrm{sp}} = I-|p_\sigma\rangle\langle
   201	  p_\sigma|$ commutes with $H_\sigma,A_\sigma$ and is contractive on both
   202	  entries of~\eqref{E:compact-spectral-phase-norm}. On its support $h \ge E_2 =
   203	  -\mu_\sigma^2$, the phase isometry gives scalar matrix entries
   204	  \[
   205	    C_t(h),\quad \sqrt{h+c}\,S_t(h),\quad
   206	    -hS_t(h)/\sqrt{h+c},\quad C_t(h).
   207	  \]
   208	  For $h \ge 0$, use $|S_t(h)| \le \min(t,h^{-1/2})$ and split $h \le 1$ from $h
   209	  \ge 1$; the lower off-diagonal entry is at most one. For $-\mu_\sigma^2 \le h
   210	  < 0$, use $|C_t(h)| \le e^{\mu_\sigma t}$ and $|S_t(h)| \le t e^{\mu_\sigma
   211	  t}$, with $|h| \le M$ and $1 \le h+c \le c$. Thus, the complementary spatial
   212	  matrix has norm at most $C(1+t)e^{\mu_\sigma t}$, including $\mu_\sigma = 0$.
   213	
   214	  The two spatial ground branches are $(p_\sigma,\pm\lambda_\sigma p_\sigma)$.
   215	  Besides $\Pi_\sigma^E$, their projections include the decaying branch
   216	  \[
   217	    (p_\sigma,-\lambda_\sigma p_\sigma)
   218	    \frac{\langle p_\sigma,u\rangle
   219	    -\langle p_\sigma,z\rangle/\lambda_\sigma}{2}.
   220	  \]
   221	  Their sum is the spatial ground projection on both phase entries. Both
   222	  projection norms are uniformly bounded in the spectral phase norm because
   223	  $\sqrt\varepsilon \le \lambda_\sigma \le \sqrt M$ and $1 \le
   224	  c-\lambda_\sigma^2 \le c$. The decaying branch has factor $e^{-\lambda_\sigma
   225	  t}$ and remains in $I-\Pi_\sigma^E$. The fractional norm equivalence now
   226	  proves the stated complement estimate for the spectral matrix.
   227	
   228	  We identify this matrix with the physical flow. The same scalar bounds at
   229	  graph levels $(A_\sigma u,A_\sigma^{1/2}z)$ give continuous solutions in
   230	  $H^2\times H^1$. These graph norms are uniformly equivalent to the Sobolev
   231	  norms: the $H^1$ case was proved above, and $A_\sigma-B = M-V_\sigma$ is
   232	  bounded by $M$ while $A_\sigma,B \ge 1$. Spectral cutoffs give $u_t = z$ in
   233	  $H^1$ and $z_t = -H_\sigma u$ in $L^2$, with continuous derivatives there. The
   234	  free Fourier group on $H^1\times L^2$ has, after its Bessel isometry, the same
   235	  bounded weighted entries and is strongly continuous by dominated Fourier
   236	  convergence. Its generator is $(z,\Delta u)$ on $H^2\times H^1$, as the
   237	  Fourier multipliers show. For compact smooth initial data, differentiating the
   238	  free interaction picture at these graph levels gives Duhamel with force
   239	  $(0,V_\sigma u)$. The identity also holds in $E$. Multiplication by $V_\sigma$
   240	  maps $H^{1/2}$ into $L^2$ and then $H^{-1/2}$ with bound $M$, so Picard
   241	  uniqueness identifies the spectral solution with the ordinary $E$ flow on
   242	  these data. Density within $E$ and finite-horizon boundedness extend equality
   243	  to all $E$. No density of $E$ in $F$ is used. Finally, the ground branches
   244	  give~\eqref{E:compact-E-eigen}; their pairings are continuous because
   245	  $p_\sigma \in H^2$. Continuity and uniform bounds of the displayed vectors and
   246	  duals follow from Proposition~\ref{P:compact-ground-family}. This proves
   247	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-E-wave}.
   248	\end{proof}

   250	\subsection{The growing projection and its complementary wave evolution}
   251	
   252	For the constant coordinates write $C(t)(c_1,c_2) = (c_1+tc_2,c_2)$ and
   253	$D_\sigma(c_1,c_2) = (0,V_\sigma c_1) \in E$.
   254	
   255	\begin{proposition}[The growing projection on the wave phase space]
   256	  \label{P:compact-F-projection}
   257	  The physical flow satisfies
   258	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-F-block}
   259	    P_\sigma(t)(e,c)
   260	    =\left(P_\sigma^E(t)e+

261	    \int_0^tP_\sigma^E(t-r)D_\sigma C(r)c\ud r,\ C(t)c\right).
   262	  \end{equation}
   263	  Set
   264	  \begin{align}
   265	    f_\sigma&=\frac{\int V_\sigma p_\sigma}{2\lambda_\sigma}>0,
   266	    &\ell_\sigma^C(c)&=
   267	    f_\sigma\left(\frac{c_1}{\lambda_\sigma}
   268	    +\frac{c_2}{\lambda_\sigma^2}\right),
   269	    \label{E:compact-constant-dual}\\
   270	    e_\sigma&=ie_\sigma^E,
   271	    &\ell_\sigma(e,c)&=\ell_\sigma^E(e)+\ell_\sigma^C(c),\qquad
   272	    \Pi_\sigma=e_\sigma\ell_\sigma,\quad Q_\sigma=I-\Pi_\sigma.
   273	    \label{E:compact-F-projection}
   274	  \end{align}
   275	  These vectors, duals and rank-one projections are norm-continuous and
   276	  uniformly bounded, and
   277	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-F-eigen}
   278	    \ell_\sigma(e_\sigma)=1,\qquad
   279	    P_\sigma(t)\Pi_\sigma=\Pi_\sigma P_\sigma(t)
   280	    =e^{\lambda_\sigma t}\Pi_\sigma.
   281	  \end{equation}
   282	  For every fixed nonnegative smooth compact $\phi$ of integral one,
   283	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-positive-margins}
   284	    \inf_I\ell_\sigma(e_0)>0,\qquad
   285	    \inf_I O_\phi(e_\sigma)>0.
   286	  \end{equation}
   287	\end{proposition}
   288	
   289	\begin{proof}
   290	  The constant coordinates obey $C(t)$ because the potential force has range in
   291	  $iE$. To justify variation of constants on the $E$ component, let $g$ be a
   292	  continuous $E$ force and substitute the ordinary free-Duhamel equation for
   293	  $P_\sigma^E(t-r)g(r)$ in its time integral. With $B_\sigma^E(u,z) =
   294	  (0,V_\sigma u)$, strong $E$-valued Fubini gives
   295	  \begin{align*}
   296	    &\int_0^t\int_r^t S(t-s)B_\sigma^E
   297	    P_\sigma^E(s-r)g(r)\ud s\ud r\\
   298	    &\qquad=\int_0^tS(t-s)B_\sigma^E
   299	    \left[\int_0^sP_\sigma^E(s-r)g(r)\ud r\right]\ud s.
   300	  \end{align*}
   301	  All norms are bounded on the finite triangle, so this exchange is absolute in
   302	  $E$. Thus, $Y(t) = P_\sigma^E(t)e+\int_0^tP_\sigma^E(t-r)g(r)\ud r$ solves
   303	  free Duhamel with force $B_\sigma^EY+g$. Take $g(r) = D_\sigma C(r)c$ and
   304	  adjoin the constant block. This is the same $F$ Duhamel equation as the
   305	  ordinary flow; uniqueness proves~\eqref{E:compact-F-block}. Its finite-horizon
   306	  bounds are uniform since the family has bounded $L^\infty$ and $L^2$ norms on
   307	  one compact support.
   308	
   309	  The integral defining $f_\sigma$ is finite by $L^2$ Cauchy--Schwarz and
   310	  positive because $V_\sigma$ is nonzero by the common trial and $p_\sigma > 0$
   311	  a.e. Its coefficients are continuous and uniformly bounded by the $H^2$
   312	  continuity and positive lower bound for the rate; no $p_\sigma \in L^1$
   313	  assumption is used. Directly,
   314	  \begin{align*}
   315	    \ell_\sigma^ED_\sigma C(r)c&=f_\sigma(c_1+rc_2),\\
   316	    \ell_\sigma^C(c)
   317	    &=\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda_\sigma r}
   318	    f_\sigma(c_1+rc_2)\ud r,\\
   319	    \ell_\sigma^C(C(t)c)
   320	    &=\int_t^\infty e^{\lambda_\sigma(t-r)}
   321	    f_\sigma(c_1+rc_2)\ud r.
   322	  \end{align*}
   323	  These integrals converge absolutely. Applying $\ell_\sigma$
   324	  to~\eqref{E:compact-F-block}, the finite integral and this tail combine to
   325	  give $\ell_\sigma P_\sigma(t) = e^{\lambda_\sigma t}\ell_\sigma$. The ground
   326	  mode also gives $P_\sigma(t)e_\sigma = e^{\lambda_\sigma t}e_\sigma$ and
   327	  $\ell_\sigma(e_\sigma) = 1$, proving~\eqref{E:compact-F-eigen}. Bounded
   328	  bilinear multiplication and the preceding continuous coefficients prove norm
   329	  continuity of all objects. Finally, $\ell_\sigma(e_0) =
   330	  f_\sigma/\lambda_\sigma > 0$ and $O_\phi(e_\sigma) = \int\phi p_\sigma > 0$.
   331	  Both are continuous on compact $I$, proving
   332	  \eqref{E:compact-positive-margins}. Positivity is in integrals, without a
   333	  point trace or a one-dimensional ODE. This proves
   334	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-F-projection}.
   335	\end{proof}
   336	
   337	\begin{proposition}[Complementary wave evolution and parameter dependence]
   338	  \label{P:compact-F-complement}
   339	  Uniformly over $\sigma$ and $t \ge 0$,
   340	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-F-complement}
   341	    \|P_\sigma(t)Q_\sigma\|_{\mathcal{B}(F)}
   342	    \le C(1+t)^3e^{\mu_\sigma t}.
   343	  \end{equation}
   344	  For every fixed $0 < \eta < d_0$,
   345	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-normalized-complement}
   346	    \|e^{-\lambda_\sigma t}P_\sigma(t)Q_\sigma\|
   347	    \le C_\eta e^{-\eta t}.
   348	  \end{equation}
   349	  For every finite $T_0$,
   350	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-parameter-flow}
   351	    \sup_{0\le t\le T_0}\|P_\sigma(t)-P_\tau(t)\|_{\mathcal{B}(F)}
   352	    \le C_{T_0}
   353	    \big(\|V_\sigma-V_\tau\|_\infty+\|V_\sigma-V_\tau\|_2\big).
   354	  \end{equation}
   355	\end{proposition}
   356	
   357	\begin{proof}
   358	  Write $Q_\sigma^E = I-\Pi_\sigma^E$. Split $D_\sigma$ into its growing and
   359	  complementary parts in~\eqref{E:compact-F-block} and use the two tail
   360	  integrals in the preceding proof. The exact $E$ component of
   361	  $P_\sigma(t)Q_\sigma(e,c)$ is
   362	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-complement-forcing}
   363	    P_\sigma^E(t)Q_\sigma^Ee
   364	    +\int_0^tP_\sigma^E(t-r)Q_\sigma^ED_\sigma C(r)c\ud r
   365	    -e_\sigma^E\ell_\sigma^C(C(t)c),
   366	  \end{equation}
   367	  and the constant component is $C(t)c$. The final subtraction retains the
   368	  growing response to constants in the projection. Since $\|Q_\sigma^ED_\sigma
   369	  C(r)\| \le C(1+r)$, the integral in~\eqref{E:compact-complement-forcing} has
   370	  norm at most
   371	  \[
   372	    Ce^{\mu_\sigma t}|c|
   373	    \int_0^t(1+t-r)(1+r)\ud r
   374	    =Ce^{\mu_\sigma t}(t+t^2+t^3/6)|c|.
   375	  \]
   376	  The first term is bounded by $C(1+t)e^{\mu_\sigma t}\|e\|_E$; the final term
   377	  and constant component by $C(1+t)|c|$. Since $\mu_\sigma \ge 0$ this proves
   378	  \eqref{E:compact-F-complement}. The boundedness of $(1+t)^3e^{-(d_0-\eta)t}$
   379	  proves \eqref{E:compact-normalized-complement}. In particular, the
   380	  constant-velocity polynomial is included in this estimate.
   381	
   382	  Put $\mathcal{B}_\sigma = iB_F(V_\sigma)$ and $d_{\sigma,\tau} =
   383	  \|V_\sigma-V_\tau\|_\infty+ \|V_\sigma-V_\tau\|_2$. The bound for $B_F$ gives
   384	  $\|\mathcal{B}_\sigma-\mathcal{B}_\tau\| \le d_{\sigma,\tau}$. Subtract the
   385	  two free-Duhamel equations on states. Their difference is the sum of the
   386	  integral with $S_F(t-r)\mathcal{B}_\sigma(P_\sigma(r)-P_\tau(r))$ and that
   387	  with $S_F(t-r)(\mathcal{B}_\sigma-\mathcal{B}_\tau)P_\tau(r)$. The uniform
   388	  finite-horizon bounds and scalar Gronwall prove
   389	  \eqref{E:compact-parameter-flow}. The operator norm is measurable:
   390	  separability of $F$ expresses it as the supremum over a countable dense set of
   391	  unit states, each with continuous image. Hence, Gronwall applies without a
   392	  $\mathcal{B}(F)$-valued derivative or operator-norm continuity of the free
   393	  group. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:compact-F-complement}.
   394	\end{proof}

   396	\subsection{The original nonnegative control and a common trial}
   397	
   398	\begin{lemma}[The original mean and variance]\label{L:compact-raw-profile}
   399	  Let $\Gamma \ne 0$ satisfy Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, let $a = \alpha_0$, and
   400	  let real nonnegative nonzero $\Psi \in C_c^\infty((0,1)\times\R^d)$ be
   401	  arbitrary, without a separability assumption. Define
   402	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-raw-mean}
   403	    h_\sigma(x)=\int_0^1|\sigma-u|^{-a}
   404	    (\Gamma*\Psi(u,\cdot))(x)\ud u,\qquad
   405	    \overline{q}(x)=\int_0^1\Psi(u,x)\ud u,\qquad Z=W(\Psi).
   406	  \end{equation}
   407	  Then $h$ is smooth in time and space on compact sets, and
   408	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-raw-cost}
   409	    0<v_\Psi:=\E Z^2
   410	    =\int_0^1\int\Psi(\sigma,x)h_\sigma(x)\ud x\ud\sigma<\infty.
   411	  \end{equation}
   412	  Against every smooth compact positive-time test $F_0$,
   413	  \[
   414	    \E[W(\Psi)W(F_0)]=\int F_0(s,x)h_s(x)\ud x\ud s.
   415	  \]
   416	  Moreover, on $I$,
   417	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-positive-mean-floor}
   418	    h_\sigma\ge\Gamma*\overline{q},\qquad
   419	    v_\Psi\ge Q(\overline{q})
   420	    :=\int\Gamma(\ud z)\int\overline{q}(x)\overline{q}(x-z)\ud x>0.
   421	  \end{equation}
   422	  For every fixed mask, $V_\sigma = m_Rh_\sigma$ is a smooth compact family,
   423	  Lipschitz in $\sigma$ in $L^\infty$ and $L^2$.
   424	\end{lemma}
   425	
   426	\begin{proof}
   427	  Choose $A \ge 1$ containing the spatial support of $\Psi$ in $B_A$. The
   428	  original covariance identity and absolute Fubini give the stated mean pairing:
   429	  the two compact tests restrict spatial differences to a compact set of finite
   430	  $\Gamma$ mass, and the time singularity is locally integrable since $a < 1$.
   431	  This identifies the linear covariance mean without evaluating noise at a
   432	  point. The same calculation gives~\eqref{E:compact-raw-cost}. Its spatial
   433	  integrand is bounded in integral by
   434	  $\|\Psi\|_\infty^2|B_A|\Gamma(\overline{B}_{2A})$, and
   435	  $\int_0^1\int_0^1|\sigma-u|^{-a}\ud u\ud\sigma = 2/((1-a)(2-a))$, proving
   436	  finiteness.
   437	
   438	  Nonnegative nonzero smooth $\Psi$ has positive integral, so $\overline{q} \ne
   439	  0$. Nonzero $\Gamma$ charges some ball, and homogeneity gives $\Gamma(B_1) =
   440	  r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(B_r) > 0$. Thus, every origin-centered ball $B_r$, $r > 0$,
   441	  has positive finite mass. The continuous compact autocorrelation
   442	  $\int\overline{q}(x)\overline{q}(x-z)\ud x$ is positive at zero and bounded
   443	  below on some ball. This proves $0 < Q(\overline{q}) < \infty$. Since
   444	  $|\sigma-u|^{-a} \ge 1$ on the unit time square, positive Tonelli gives both
   445	  inequalities in~\eqref{E:compact-positive-mean-floor}.
   446	
   447	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time and write
   448	  \[
   449	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
   450	    \int\Gamma(\ud z)\Psi(s-r,x-z)\ud r.
   451	  \]
   452	  On compact $s,x$ sets the relevant $r,z$ range over fixed compact sets;
   453	  $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable there. Every derivative falls on the smooth test, not
   454	  on the singular time kernel. Dominated differentiation gives smoothness and
   455	  continuity of all derivatives on compacts. Multiplication by $m_R$ now gives
   456	  the claimed compact family and its fixed-$R$ Lipschitz bounds. This proves
   457	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}.
   458	\end{proof}
   459	
   460	\begin{proposition}[Binding with the original control and cost fixed]
   461	  \label{P:compact-original-common-trial}
   462	  For every $\Psi$ in Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}, a sufficiently large
   463	  finite mask $m_R$ gives $V_\sigma = m_Rh_\sigma$ a common negative
   464	  trial~\eqref{E:compact-common-trial}. Thus, all preceding ground, projection,
   465	  positive-margin and complementary-wave conclusions apply. The rate is
   466	  Lipschitz on $I$ and has $\lambda_0 > 0$. The original test $\Psi$, original
   467	  variable $Z$ and variance $v_\Psi$ are unchanged by this choice. The mask can
   468	  additionally cover any fixed compact variational test supports.
   469	\end{proposition}
   470	
   471	\begin{proof}
   472	  Choose a real unit $L^2$ function $\psi \in C_c^\infty(B_2)$ with $\psi \ge
   473	  c_0 > 0$ on $B_1$, and put $\psi_L(x) = L^{-d/2}\psi(x/L)$, $D_\psi =
   474	  \|\nabla\psi\|_2^2$, where $L \ge \max(1,2A)$. Choose the even mask with $R
   475	  \ge 2L$, so $V_\sigma = h_\sigma$ on $\operatorname{supp}\psi_L$. This is the
   476	  allowed real mask $0 \le m_R \le 1$, equal to one on $B_R$ and with support in
   477	  $\overline{B}_{2R}$. Positive Tonelli
   478	  and~\eqref{E:compact-positive-mean-floor} give
   479	  \begin{align}
   480	    \int V_\sigma\psi_L^2
   481	    &\ge c_0^2L^{-d}\int_{B_L}(\Gamma*\overline{q})(x)\ud x\nonumber\\
   482	    &=c_0^2L^{-d}\int\overline{q}(y)\Gamma(B_L-y)\ud y\nonumber\\
   483	    &\ge c_0^2L^{-d}\Gamma(B_{L/2})\int\overline{q}
   484	    =C_\Gamma L^{-\alpha},\label{E:compact-trial-potential}\\
   485	    C_\Gamma&=c_0^22^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(B_1)\int\overline{q}>0.\nonumber
   486	  \end{align}
   487	  Here $B_{L/2} \subset B_L-y$ for $|y| \le A$ and $L \ge 2A$. All covariance
   488	  masses in the argument are compact and finite. The kinetic energy is $D_\psi
   489	  L^{-2}$. Since $\alpha < 2$, choose $L$ large enough that $\varepsilon_R: =
   490	  C_\Gamma L^{-\alpha}-D_\psi L^{-2} > 0$. Then
   491	  \[
   492	    \|\nabla\psi_L\|_2^2-\int V_\sigma\psi_L^2
   493	    \le-\varepsilon_R\quad\hbox{for every }\sigma\in I.
   494	  \]
   495	  Fix this finite $R$ before invoking Proposition~\ref{P:compact-ground-family}.
   496	  Its level bound and the mean Lipschitz estimate give
   497	  \[
   498	    |\lambda_\sigma-\lambda_\tau|
   499	    \le\frac{\|V_\sigma-V_\tau\|_\infty}{2\sqrt{\varepsilon_R}}
   500	    \le C_R|\sigma-\tau|.
   501	  \]
   502	  The positive mean integrates the entire time test, so $\lambda_0 > 0$ even
   503	  though $\Psi(0,\cdot) = 0$. Only the trial and mask have grown; the original
   504	  test, its variable and~\eqref{E:compact-raw-cost} were fixed first. Enlarging
   505	  $R$ to contain additional fixed compact test supports preserves the trial and
   506	  gives equality of masked and unmasked potential energies on those supports.
   507	  This includes singular invariant-direction covariances and the one-dimensional
   508	  white case. It is not an all-strength binding assertion for one fixed compact
   509	  potential. Masks are fixed before source or time asymptotics; a later supremum
   510	  over controls must follow their individual bounds. This proves
   511	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial}.
   512	\end{proof}

   114	\begin{proposition}[Change of law on the whole norm-Borel space]
   115	  \label{P:raw-block-gaussian-law}
   116	  For every nonnegative norm-Borel $j$ on all of $\mathscr{B}_\delta$,
   117	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-gaussian-law}
   118	    \E j(X)=
   119	    \E\left[e^{-Z/\sqrt\delta-v/(2\delta)}j(X+H)\right].
   120	  \end{equation}
   121	  The equality is valid also as an extended nonnegative integral.
   122	\end{proposition}
   123	
   124	\begin{proof}
   125	  For real $s$, the density $e^{-sZ-s^2v/2}$ defines an equivalent probability
   126	  measure $Q_s$ by completing the square in the $N(0,v)$ density. For any finite
   127	  list $\ell$ of continuous real coordinates on $\mathscr{B}_\delta$, the
   128	  Gaussian vector $(\ell(X),Z)$ is equal in law to $(TG,z\cdot G)$ for a finite
   129	  standard Gaussian vector $G$. A positive covariance square root gives this
   130	  representation even when singular; no inverse is used. Here $Tz = \ell(b)$ and
   131	  $|z|^2 = v$. Substitution $G' = G+sz$ in its density gives
   132	  $\E_{Q_s}f(\ell(X+sb)) = \E f(\ell(X))$ for every bounded Borel $f$.
   133	
   134	  The matrix entries of each block in a real Hilbert basis at rational times,
   135	  together with $0,B$, generate the norm-Borel sigma-field. To see the
   136	  operator-norm point, for a countable dense set $\mathcal{D}$ of unit vectors
   137	  obtained from normalized rational finite basis combinations, $\|T\| =
   138	  \sup_{u,w\in\mathcal{D}}|\langle Tu,w\rangle|$. These pairings are finite
   139	  linear combinations of matrix entries. Supremum and H\"older norms of
   140	  continuous paths are suprema over rational times and pairs. Thus, distance to
   141	  every fixed element of $\mathscr{B}_\delta$ is coordinate-measurable. Open
   142	  balls are measurable by rational closed-ball approximation, and separability
   143	  makes every open set a countable union of balls from dense centers. Conversely
   144	  the coordinates are continuous. The cylinder sets form a generating pi-system;
   145	  uniqueness of probability measures extends the finite-coordinate equality to
   146	  all norm-Borel sets. Simple functions and monotone convergence give the
   147	  identity for nonnegative $j$. Finally, take $s = \delta^{-1/2}$ and use $sb =
   148	  H$ from~\eqref{E:raw-block-covariance}. The map and its deterministic
   149	  translate are defined on the entire input space; there is no translated
   150	  exceptional-domain assumption. This proves
   151	  Proposition~\ref{P:raw-block-gaussian-law}.
   152	\end{proof}

   161	\begin{lemma}[Uniform block error]\label{L:raw-block-uniform-error}
   162	  Let $M_\delta = \max_{m\le N}\|X_m\|_{\mathscr{B}_0}$, including its factor
   163	  $g_\delta$. Then $M_\delta \to 0$ in every finite $L^q$, and, for some $c >
   164	  0$,
   165	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-maximum-exponential}
   166	    \sup_\delta\E e^{cM_\delta^2}<\infty.
   167	  \end{equation}
   168	  With the deterministic $P_s$ in~\eqref{E:compact-F-block},
   169	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-operator-error}
   170	    E_{\mathrm{op},\delta}:=
   171	    \max_{m\le N}\sup_{0\le u\le B}
   172	    \|D_m^+(u)-P_{s_m}(u)\|_{\mathcal{B}(F)}
   173	    \longrightarrow0
   174	    \quad\hbox{in every finite }L^q.
   175	  \end{equation}
   176	\end{lemma}
   177	
   178	\begin{proof}
   179	  The maximum and~\eqref{E:raw-block-moments}, with $N+1 \le 2/\delta$, give
   180	  \[
   181	    \|M_\delta\|_p
   182	    \le (N+1)^{1/p}C\sqrt p\,g_\delta
   183	    \le C'\sqrt p\,\delta^{(1-a)/2-1/p}.
   184	  \]
   185	  For fixed $q$, choose $p > \max(q,2/(1-a))$ to prove the first limit. No
   186	  independence is needed. Choose an integer $n_0$ with $n_0(1-a) \ge 1$. For $n
   187	  \ge n_0$,
   188	  \[
   189	    \E M_\delta^{2n}
   190	    \le2C^{2n}(2n)^n\delta^{n(1-a)-1}
   191	    \le2C^{2n}(2n)^n.
   192	  \]
   193	  For $1 \le n < n_0$, Lyapunov bounds the moment by the appropriate power of
   194	  the $2n_0$ moment. These finitely many terms are bounded. For the remaining
   195	  exponential series, $n! \ge (n/e)^n$ gives a geometric tail $2\sum_{n\ge
   196	  n_0}(2ecC^2)^n$ for small $c$. This
   197	  proves~\eqref{E:raw-block-maximum-exponential}; no such assertion is made for
   198	  the unscaled maximum.
   199	
   200	  Let $H_m^{\mathrm{stat}}$ be the primitive for constant potential $V_{s_m}$.
   201	  Compact mea smoothness on $[0,2]$ and the statewise primitive bound give
   202	  \[
   203	    \sup_m\max(\|H_m\|_{C^\theta},
   204	    \|H_m^{\mathrm{stat}}\|_{C^\theta})\le H_0,\qquad
   205	    \sup_m\|H_m-H_m^{\mathrm{stat}}\|_{C^\theta}\le C\delta.
   206	  \]

   208	  $L^2$; integration of the bounded free groups gives its Lipschitz primitive
   209	  bound on this fixed horizon. On $\{M_\delta\le1\}$, local Young stability on
   210	  the fixed ball of radius $H_0+1$ gives $E_{\mathrm{op},\delta} \le
   211	  C(M_\delta+\delta)$. This proves convergence in probability. The global Young
   212	  bound also gives
   213	  \[
   214	    \max_m\sup_{u\le B}\|D_m^+(u)\|
   215	    \le C_B\exp\big(C_B(1+H_0+M_\delta)^{1/\theta}\big).
   216	  \]
   217	  Since $1/\theta < 2$, every finite power of this bound is dominated by a
   218	  constant times the exponential in~\eqref{E:raw-block-maximum-exponential}.
   219	  Uniform higher moments yield uniform integrability, proving
   220	  \eqref{E:raw-block-operator-error}. Suprema are measurable: on a countable
   221	  dense set of unit states each difference is continuous in $u$, so rational
   222	  times and those states suffice. Operator-norm continuity of the physical free
   223	  group is not used. Only $s_m \le 1$ supplies the ground templates. This proves
   224	  Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-uniform-error}.

227	\begin{lemma}[Indexed cone and terminal displacement]
   228	  \label{L:raw-block-indexed-cone}

   230	  $\omega,\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}},c_*$ such that the following holds for every $N
   231	  \ge 1$. If $\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_N \in I$ have adjacent distances at most
   232	  $\omega$ and real bounded operator families $D_m(u)$, $0 \le u \le B$, satisfy
   233	  \[

   238	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-positive-product}

   240	    \ge c_*(1-\varrho)^{N-1}
   241	    \exp\left(B\sum_{m<N}\lambda_{\sigma_m}
   242	    +u\lambda_{\sigma_N}\right)>0.
   243	  \end{equation}

   245	  required.

   247	
   248	\begin{proof}
   249	  From~\eqref{E:compact-normalized-complement} fix $C_{\mathrm{gap}} \ge 1$,
   250	  $\eta_{\mathrm{gap}} > 0$ so the normalized complementary norm is at most
   251	  $C_{\mathrm{gap}}e^{-\eta_{\mathrm{gap}}t}$. Define positive margins and
   252	  finite bounds
   253	  \[
   254	    a_*=\inf_I\ell_s(e_0),\quad j_*=\inf_I O_\phi(e_s),\quad
   255	    M_e=\max(1,\sup_I\|e_s\|),\quad
   256	    M_\ell=\max(1,\sup_I\|\ell_s\|).
   257	  \]
   258	  Also put $M_P = \max(1,\sup_I\|\Pi_s\|)$, $M_Q = 1+M_P$, $M_z = M_e+1$, $E_0 =
   259	  \|e_0\| = 1$ and $H_{\mathrm{obs}} = \max(1,\|O_\phi\|)$. Choose the aperture
   260	  \emph{first}: $\vartheta = \min(1,j_*/(16H_{\mathrm{obs}}C_{\mathrm{gap}})) >
   261	  0$. Next choose integer $B \ge 1$ with
   262	  \[
   263	    q_B:=C_{\mathrm{gap}}e^{-\eta_{\mathrm{gap}}B}
   264	    \le\min\left(\frac18,\frac{\vartheta a_*}{8M_QE_0}\right).
   265	  \]

   267	  Uniform continuity of $\ell_s,\Pi_s$ supplies $\omega > 0$ for which adjacent
   268	  distances at most $\omega$ give both norm differences at most $\nu$. Finally,
   269	  choose $\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}} > 0$ satisfying all five smallness conditions
   270	  \begin{align*}
   271	    M_\ell\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}M_z&\le\varrho/2,&
   272	    M_Q\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}M_z&\le\vartheta/4,\\
   273	    M_\ell\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}E_0&\le a_*/2,&
   274	    M_Q\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}E_0&\le\vartheta a_*/8,&
   275	    H_{\mathrm{obs}}\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}M_z&\le j_*/8.
   276	  \end{align*}
   277	  All denominators are positive. This order of choices uses the normalized
   278	  complement rather than a growing terminal norm.
   279	
   280	  The cone at $s$ consists of $z = Ae_s+r$, with $A = \ell_s(z) > 0$, $\ell_s(r)
   281	  = 0$ and $\|r\|_F \le \vartheta A$. In particular, $r = Q_sz$ and $\|z\| \le
   282	  M_zA$. For entrance, $z_1 = D_0(B)e_0$, with $b = \sigma_0$, has normalized
   283	  amplitude at least $a_*-M_\ell\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}E_0 \ge a_*/2$. Its
   284	  normalized residual is at most $q_BM_QE_0+M_Q\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}E_0 \le
   285	  \vartheta a_*/4$. Thus, it enters the cone with residual ratio at most
   286	  $\vartheta/2$ and amplitude at least $e^{\lambda_bB}a_*/2$.
   287	
   288	  For an old-cone state $z = Ae_b+r$ and an adjacent index $c$, rebase before
   289	  using the complementary estimate:
   290	  \[
   291	    \ell_c(z)\ge(1-\nu M_z)A,\qquad
   292	    \|Q_cz\|\le\|Q_bz\|+\|(\Pi_b-\Pi_c)z\|
   293	    \le(\vartheta+\nu M_z)A.
   294	  \]

   296	  e^{-\lambda_cB}\ell_c(Dz)$ and $y = e^{-\lambda_cB}\|Q_cDz\|$. Since

   301	  \]

   304	    y\le

   333	\begin{lemma}[Composition over time blocks and regularized products]
   334	  \label{L:raw-block-restart}
   335	  Fix $\delta,B,N$ and let $L = \delta^{-1}$, $L_{\mathrm{ext}} = (N+1)B \ge L$.
   336	  On this global fast horizon define $A_{\mathrm{glob}} = g_\delta
   337	  A_R(W_{\mathrm{fast}})$. Its physical flow obeys
   338	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-restart}
   339	    P_{\mathrm{glob}}(mB+u,mB)=D_m^0(u),\qquad 0\le u\le B.
   340	  \end{equation}
   341	  The analogous identity holds with the deterministic mean $V_{\delta t}$ added
   342	  globally and local operator paths $X_m+H_m$. Their finite block products,
   343	  including the last remainder $\tau$, are source limits in $L^2$, at this fixed
   344	  $\delta,N$.
   345	\end{lemma}
   346	
   347	\begin{proof}
   348	  Take one regularized slow noise preserving the given noise $Y_{\epsilon,\eta}$
   349	  on the extension of the given $W$ constructed in
   350	  Section~\ref{S:source-driver-convergence}. Define the fast and local noises by
   351	  \[
   352	    Y_{\mathrm{fast}}(f)=Y_{\epsilon,\eta}(T_{\delta,0}f),\qquad
   353	    Y_m(f)=Y_{\epsilon,\eta}(T_{\delta,m}f).
   354	  \]
   355	  The pullback isometry and~\eqref{E:source-two-dominations} give source and
   356	  residual variance bounds by $\|f\|_{H_W}^2$. The residual tends to zero on
   357	  each transformed smooth compact test at fixed $\delta,m$. Joint Gaussianity is
   358	  retained. Proposition~\ref{P:source-gaussian-transfer} therefore gives the
   359	  $L^pC^\theta$ operator-path limits on $[0,L_{\mathrm{ext}}]$ and on $[0,B]$,
   360	  including both constant columns.
   361	
   362	  Their random fields are $Y_{\mathrm{fast}}(u,x) =
   363	  \delta^{a/2}Y_{\epsilon,\eta}(\delta u,x)$ and $Y_m(u,x) =
   364	  Y_{\mathrm{fast}}(mB+u,x)$. Indeed, these follow by change of variables in
   365	  their test integrals. The temporal law is $K_{\eta/\delta}$ because
   366	  $\delta^aK_\eta(\delta r) = K_{\eta/\delta}(r)$; the spatial heat law and all
   367	  joint width rules are unchanged. They are continuous in time and smooth in
   368	  space. Their ordinary primitives equal their Gaussian operator paths: their
   369	  matrix entries are $Y_m(h_R)$, by the indicator approximation used
   370	  in~\eqref{E:raw-block-mean-jacobian} and the point-test integral identity.
   371	  Total finite propagation extends this identity to both constant columns. This
   372	  does not assume a separately chosen extension preserving the given noise
   373	  automatically commutes with time dilation.
   374	
   375	  Changing the ordinary source integration variable and composing the free
   376	  groups gives the exact identity on $F$
   377	  \[
   378	    S_F(mB)\big[A_{\mathrm{glob}}^{\mathrm{src}}(mB+u)
   379	    -A_{\mathrm{glob}}^{\mathrm{src}}(mB)\big]
   380	    S_F(-mB)=X_m^{\mathrm{src}}(u).
   381	  \]
   382	  No physical mask is commuted through a wave group. Restriction, difference and
   383	  conjugation are bounded maps on these fixed-horizon $C^\theta$ spaces. Passing
   384	  the source limits gives the same identity for $A_{\mathrm{glob}},X_m$. For the
   385	  finitely many $m$, a convergent subsequence or rational times and path
   386	  continuity gives simultaneous identities in $u$. Conjugation norms need only
   387	  be finite at this fixed $\delta$.
   388	
   389	  Conjugate the global interaction Young equation on $[mB,mB+u]$ by $S_F(mB)$.
   390	  Bounded linearity of its Riemann sums and that original identity give the
   391	  local equation driven by $X_m$. Uniqueness identifies it with $U_{X_m}$,
   392	  proving \eqref{E:raw-block-restart}. The ordinary deterministic primitive for
   393	  $V_{\delta t}$ has the identical cocycle with local $H_m$. Composition now
   394	  identifies the full product, with terminal $\tau$.
   395	
   396	  For completeness, source convergence of these finite products requires no
   397	  growing-product stability assertion. At fixed $\delta,N$ let $C \ge 1$ be the
   398	  maximum norm of their source and original factors, and let $e_{\mathrm{src}}$
   399	  be the maximum factor difference. The parent Young convergence gives every
   400	  finite moment of $C$ uniformly in source widths and $e_{\mathrm{src}} \to 0$
   401	  in every finite $L^p$. If $d(n)$ is the difference of the first $n$ ordered
   402	  products, then
   403	  \[
   404	    d(n+1)\le C d(n)+C^n e_{\mathrm{src}},\qquad d(0)=0.
   405	  \]
   406	  Extend both finite sequences by identities so the recurrence holds for all
   407	  natural $n$. The finite error-accumulation estimate gives $d(N+1) \le
   408	  (N+1)C^{N+1}e_{\mathrm{src}}$. H\"older, using $C$ in $L^{4(N+1)}$ and the
   409	  error in $L^4$, proves $L^2$ convergence. This is only a fixed-$\delta$ source
   410	  limit. Shifted source products may use the fixed original mean plus the
   411	  regularized noise; no finite-source Cameron mean is substituted. This proves
   412	  Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-restart}.
   413	\end{proof}

   417	\begin{proposition}[The square observable and canonical comparison]
   418	  \label{P:raw-block-point-comparison}
   419	  Define the signed averages without and with the deterministic mean
   420	  \[
   421	    U_{\delta,B}
   422	    =O_\phi D_N^0(\tau)D_{N-1}^0(B)\cdots D_0^0(B)e_0,
   423	    \qquad
   424	    Y_{\delta,B}
   425	    =O_\phi D_N^+(\tau)D_{N-1}^+(B)\cdots D_0^+(B)e_0.
   426	  \]
   427	  They have all finite unweighted moments, and
   428	  \begin{align}
   429	    \E U_{\delta,B}^2
   430	    &=\E\left[e^{-Z/\sqrt\delta-v/(2\delta)}
   431	    Y_{\delta,B}^2\right],
   432	    \label{E:raw-block-square-identity}\\
   433	    \E U_{\delta,B}^2
   434	    &\le\E|V_\delta(1,0)|^2
   435	    =\E|u(T,0)|^2,\qquad \delta=T^{-\kappa}.
   436	    \label{E:raw-block-original-comparison}
   437	  \end{align}
   438	  The variance $v$ in the density is the original slow original variance.
   439	\end{proposition}
   440	
   441	\begin{proof}
   442	  On all of $\mathscr{B}_\delta$ put
   443	  \[
   444	    j_\delta(x)=
   445	    |O_\phi D_{x_N}(\tau)D_{x_{N-1}}(B)\cdots D_{x_0}(B)e_0|^2.
   446	  \]
   447	  The everywhere-defined continuous Young map, fixed-time bounded free groups,
   448	  finite products and bounded $O_\phi$ make $j_\delta$ continuous and
   449	  nonnegative on the whole input space. Apply
   450	  Proposition~\ref{P:raw-block-gaussian-law} directly to these original paths.

451	  Since $X+H$ is its exact translate, this proves
   452	  \eqref{E:raw-block-square-identity} with the single original $Z = W(\Psi)$ and
   453	  its variance $v$. Finite products of the local Young flows have every finite
   454	  unweighted moment by their Gaussian path bounds and H\"older, at fixed
   455	  $\delta,N$. The Gaussian identity itself did not require prior integrability
   456	  of $j_\delta$. No source convergence under its exponential density is used.
   457	
   458	  To apply the masked comparison at the amplitude, put $\Gamma_\delta =
   459	  g_\delta^2\Gamma$ and $W' = g_\delta W_{\mathrm{fast}}$. This is a nonzero
   460	  member of the same admissible covariance class, with unchanged degree $\alpha$
   461	  and temporal parameter $a$. Its integrated operator is $g_\delta$ times the
   462	  original one: the original matrix forms are linear in noise, and
   463	  basis-independent Gaussian transfer and the bounded $F$ extension retain both
   464	  constant columns. The $n$th source chain is multiplied by $g_\delta^n$. Thus,
   465	  this is exactly the model without the deterministic mean at that amplitude.
   466	
   467	  We verify the source-limit premise of the masked comparison. Keep $\delta,B,N$
   468	  fixed and use the single regularized noise preserving the given noise of
   469	  Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-restart}. For $m < N$ let $F_m = D_m^0(B)$ and put $F_N
   470	  = D_N^0(\tau)$; write $F_{m,\rho}$ for the corresponding ordinary source
   471	  factors, where both source widths in $\rho$ tend to zero.
   472	  Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-restart} and Proposition~\ref{P:constant-gaussian-flow}
   473	  give factor convergence in every finite $L^q$ and uniform bounds for every
   474	  finite moment of their norms. These statements are on the fixed finite
   475	  horizons $[0,(N+1)B]$ and $[0,B]$, and include both constant-response columns.
   476	  Set $n = N+1$ and
   477	  \[
   478	    C_\rho=\max\left(1,\max_{m\le N}\|F_{m,\rho}\|,
   479	    \max_{m\le N}\|F_m\|\right),\qquad
   480	    e_\rho=\max_{m\le N}\|F_{m,\rho}-F_m\|.
   481	  \]
   482	  Then $\sup_\rho\|C_\rho\|_q < \infty$ for every finite $q$, and $\|e_\rho\|_q
   483	  \to 0$. Telescoping the ordered products gives
   484	  \[
   485	    \|F_{N,\rho}\cdots F_{0,\rho}-F_N\cdots F_0\|
   486	    \le n C_\rho^n e_\rho.
   487	  \]
   488	  Therefore, H\"older with exponents $4n$ and $4$ gives
   489	  \[
   490	    \big\|F_{N,\rho}\cdots F_{0,\rho}-F_N\cdots F_0\big\|_{L^2}
   491	    \le n\|C_\rho\|_{L^{4n}}^n\|e_\rho\|_{L^4}
   492	    \longrightarrow0.
   493	  \]
   494	  No uniform estimate in the growing number $N$ is needed: this source limit is
   495	  completed at each fixed $\delta,N$. The physical source identification in
   496	  Lemma~\ref{L:constant-source-solution}, with the same $m_R$ and initial state
   497	  $e_0$, identifies the source product with the tested ordinary masked solution
   498	  at fast time $L = 1/\delta$. Boundedness of $O_\phi$ and $\|e_0\| = 1$ thus
   499	  identify $U_{\delta,B}$ as its $L^2$ limit. The sources $g_\delta
   500	  Y_{\mathrm{fast}}$ have the correct law, contraction and original-test limit
   501	  by Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-restart}.
   502	
   503	  At positive source widths, $0 \le m_R \le 1$ multiplies each nonnegative
   504	  displacement Wick integrand by the product of its vertex masks. Positive Green
   505	  measures and covariance retain this comparison for unequal, self and empty
   506	  chains as well. Proposition~\ref{P:masked-source-moments} gives the tested
   507	  comparison, and the just-proved $L^2$ convergence discharges the premise of
   508	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-canonical-transfer} at $\Gamma_\delta$. Its
   509	  canonical unmasked moment limit uses the fixed-order joint source limits and
   510	  the absolutely summable order bounds. Since $\phi \ge 0$ and $\int\phi = 1$,
   511	  these facts give
   512	  \[
   513	    \E U_{\delta,B}^2
   514	    \le\E|u_{\Gamma_\delta}(L,0)|^2.
   515	  \]
   516	  Only the source products without the deterministic mean were needed for this
   517	  passage. The shifted original product is already the everywhere-defined
   518	  $j_\delta(X+H)$ in the Gaussian identity; no tilted source limit or change of
   519	  the original slow $\Psi,Z,v$ has been made.
   520	
   521	  The ordinary change from fast $u$ to slow $t = \delta u$, with phase
   522	  $(V,\delta V_t)$, transforms the unmasked source equation into the regularized
   523	  version of~\eqref{E:exact-fast-equation}, with slow terminal time one. Indeed,
   524	  $g_\delta Y_{\mathrm{fast}}(u) = \sqrt\delta\,Y_{\epsilon,\eta}(\delta u)$,
   525	  and its fast cutoff is $\eta/\delta$. The canonical fixed-order and absolutely
   526	  convergent series construction passes this law identity at fixed $\delta$ to
   527	  the original moment, preserving every mixed, unequal, self and empty chain.
   528	  Lemma~\ref{L:exact-canonical-scaling} gives the final equality
   529	  in~\eqref{E:raw-block-original-comparison}. The physical scale $r_T = T\delta$
   530	  is distinct from the fixed mask radius $R$. The mask need not contain the
   531	  growing backward cone: the comparison is a moment inequality, not equality of
   532	  masked and full fields. All source limits preceded this large-time comparison.
   533	  This proves Proposition~\ref{P:raw-block-point-comparison}.
   534	\end{proof}
   535	
   536	\begin{proposition}[Original point lower rate at the Gaussian quadratic cost]
   537	  \label{P:raw-block-original-lower}
   538	  For every original positive $\Psi$ and eligible fixed mask $R$ chosen above,
   539	  and every fixed $x \in \R^d$,
   540	  \begin{equation}\label{E:raw-block-original-lower}
   541	    \liminf_{T\to\infty}T^{-\kappa}\log\E|u(T,x)|^2
   542	    \ge 2\int_0^1\lambda_s\ud s-\frac{v_\Psi}{2}.
   543	  \end{equation}
   544	\end{proposition}
   545	
   546	\begin{proof}
   547	  Fix $e_{\mathrm{rate}} > 0$. Choose $0 < \varrho < 1/2$ with $\log(1-\varrho)
   548	  > -e_{\mathrm{rate}}/3$, then choose the cone constants, including an integer
   549	  $B$ fixed independently of $\delta$, from
   550	  Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-indexed-cone}. The control $\Psi$ and eligible mask $R$
   551	  remain fixed throughout.
   552	
   553	  Choose a finite $p > 2/(1-a)$ and put $\gamma_p = p(1-a)/2-1 > 0$.
   554	  From~\eqref{E:raw-block-moments} and $N+1 \le 2/\delta$, Markov and the union
   555	  bound give, for $\eta > 0$,
   556	  \[
   557	    \begin{split}
   558	      \mathbb{P}(M_\delta>\eta)
   559	      &\le\eta^{-p}\sum_{m=0}^N
   560	      \E\|X_m\|_{C^\theta}^p\\
   561	      &\le A_p\eta^{-p}\delta^{\gamma_p},\qquad
   562	      A_p=2(C_{R,B}\sqrt p)^p<\infty.
   563	    \end{split}
   564	  \]
   565	  This estimate concerns the coupled blocks; no independence is needed. At these
   566	  fixed data $A_p$ is independent of $\delta$.
   567	
   568	  We also specify the deterministic tolerance used with this bound. The
   569	  primitive estimates in Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-uniform-error} give, for the
   570	  constant-potential primitives $H_m^{\mathrm{stat}}$,
   571	  \[
   572	    \max_m\max(\|H_m\|_{C^\theta},
   573	    \|H_m^{\mathrm{stat}}\|_{C^\theta})\le H_0,\qquad
   574	    \max_m\|H_m-H_m^{\mathrm{stat}}\|_{C^\theta}\le C_B\delta.
   575	  \]
   576	  Apply Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear} on the fixed ball of operator
   577	  paths of radius $H_0+1$ and use the bounded free groups on $[0,B]$. There is
   578	  $L_B \ge 1$, depending on these fixed $R,B,\Psi$ and the admissible exponents,
   579	  such that on $\{M_\delta\le1\}$,
   580	  \[
   581	    E_{\mathrm{op},\delta}\le L_B(M_\delta+\delta).
   582	  \]
   583	  Set $\eta = \min(1,\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}/(2L_B)) > 0$. If $\delta \le
   584	  \epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}/(2L_B)$, then $M_\delta \le \eta$ implies
   585	  $E_{\mathrm{op},\delta} \le \epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}$. Thus, for the measurable
   586	  event on the original common space
   587	  \[
   588	    E_\delta=\{E_{\mathrm{op},\delta}\le\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}\}
   589	    \cap\{|Z|\le\delta^{-1/4}\},\qquad
   590	    p_\delta=\mathbb{P}(E_\delta),
   591	  \]
   592	  Chebyshev for the same single $Z = W(\Psi)$, with $\E Z^2 = v$, gives
   593	  \[
   594	    p_\delta\ge1-A_p\eta^{-p}\delta^{\gamma_p}
   595	    -v\delta^{1/2}\longrightarrow1.
   596	  \]
   597	  This is one union bound, with no independence between blocks or from $Z$ and
   598	  no product of block probabilities.
   599	
   600	  Let $C_\lambda$ be a Lipschitz bound for $s\mapsto\lambda_s$. Take $\delta$
   601	  small enough, in addition to $0 < \delta < \min(1,1/B)$, that
   602	  \[
   603	    \begin{gathered}
   604	      \delta B\le\omega,\qquad
   605	      \delta\le\epsilon_{\mathrm{op}}/(2L_B),\qquad
   606	      C_\lambda\delta B\le e_{\mathrm{rate}}/3,\\
   607	      \delta|\log c_*|\le e_{\mathrm{rate}}/3,\qquad
   608	      A_p\eta^{-p}\delta^{\gamma_p}+v\delta^{1/2}\le1/2.
   609	    \end{gathered}
   610	  \]
   611	  Every constant has been fixed before this choice. The condition involving
   612	  $C_\lambda$ is vacuous if that constant is zero. All source limits in
   613	  Proposition~\ref{P:raw-block-point-comparison} have already been completed at
   614	  each such fixed $\delta$.
   615	
   616	  The indices $s_m = m\delta B$ lie in $I$ with adjacent gaps at most $\omega$.
   617	  On $E_\delta$ the shifted full-$F$ blocks therefore satisfy
   618	  Lemma~\ref{L:raw-block-indexed-cone}, retaining both phase entries and the
   619	  final remainder $\tau$. In particular, $Y_{\delta,B} > 0$, and
   620	  \[
   621	    \delta\log Y_{\delta,B}
   622	    \ge\delta\log c_*+\delta(N-1)\log(1-\varrho)
   623	    +\delta B\sum_{m<N}\lambda_{s_m}
   624	    +\delta\tau\lambda_{s_N}.
   625	  \]
   626	  Since $s_N+\delta\tau = 1$, the last two terms are the left Riemann sum for
   627	  $I_R$ on the entire interval, including its last interval of length
   628	  $\delta\tau$, with mesh at most $\delta B$. Its error is at most
   629	  $C_\lambda\delta B$. Also $0 \le \delta(N-1) \le 1/B \le 1$, so the
   630	  logarithmic loss is at least $\log(1-\varrho) > -e_{\mathrm{rate}}/3$. The two
   631	  other losses are each at most $e_{\mathrm{rate}}/3$ by the choices above.
   632	  Hence,
   633	  \[
   634	    Y_{\delta,B}\ge
   635	    \exp((I_R-e_{\mathrm{rate}})/\delta)\quad\hbox{on }E_\delta,
   636	  \]
   637	  including the $N = 1$ and $\tau = 0$ cases of the cone estimate.
   638	
   639	  The integrand in~\eqref{E:raw-block-square-identity} is nonnegative. On the
   640	  same $E_\delta$ its linear Gaussian term satisfies $-Z/\sqrt\delta \ge
   641	  -\delta^{-3/4}$. Restriction to this event
   642	  and~\eqref{E:raw-block-original-comparison} therefore give the explicit bound
   643	  for the original point moment
   644	  \[
   645	    \E|u(T,0)|^2\ge\E U_{\delta,B}^2
   646	    \ge p_\delta\exp\left(
   647	    \frac{2I_R-2e_{\mathrm{rate}}-v/2}{\delta}
   648	    -\delta^{-3/4}\right),\qquad \delta=T^{-\kappa}.
   649	  \]
   650	  Here $p_\delta \ge 1/2$ for small $\delta$, so $-\delta\log2 \le \delta\log
   651	  p_\delta \le 0$. Multiplying the logarithm of the preceding inequality by
   652	  $\delta$ yields
   653	  \[
   654	    \delta\log\E|u(T,0)|^2
   655	    \ge2I_R-2e_{\mathrm{rate}}-v/2
   656	    -\delta^{1/4}+\delta\log p_\delta.
   657	  \]
   658	  Thus, the normalized linear penalty is $\delta\delta^{-3/4} = \delta^{1/4} \to
   659	  0$, and $\delta\log p_\delta \to 0$. The quadratic Gaussian cost is precisely
   660	  half the original variance $v$. Since $\kappa > 0$, $\delta = T^{-\kappa}$ is
   661	  a bijection between all sufficiently large $T$ and all sufficiently small
   662	  $\delta$. This gives the full continuous-time liminf $Q_2 \ge
   663	  2I_R-2e_{\mathrm{rate}}-v/2$. For each $e_{\mathrm{rate}}$ the argument first
   664	  fixed its own $B = B(e_{\mathrm{rate}})$ and then took $\delta\downarrow0$.
   665	  The original point rate $Q_2$ is independent of $B$; only now let
   666	  $e_{\mathrm{rate}}\downarrow0$. No choice $B = B(\delta)$ is made.
   667	
   668	  Finally, spatial translation of all positive-width vertices preserves the
   669	  original noise law, Green kernels and constant initial data. The fixed-order
   670	  $L^2$ and absolute-series limits preserve equality of point second moments.
   671	  Hence, zero can be replaced by every fixed $x$
   672	  in~\eqref{E:raw-block-original-lower}. Every control and mask were fixed
   673	  before asymptotics; a supremum over them may follow their individual
   674	  inequalities. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:raw-block-original-lower}.
   675	\end{proof}

    72	/-- The family-parameter interval `I = [0,1]` of `S:compact-mean-family`
    73	(TeX `integrated_compact_mean_family.tex`, line 4). -/
    74	def paramI : Set ℝ := Icc 0 1
    75	
    76	/-- `I = [0,1]` is compact (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
    77	theorem isCompact_paramI : IsCompact paramI := isCompact_Icc

    79	/-- The C16 outputs used by `L:raw-block-indexed-cone`, supplied as one
    80	hypothesis structure (inputs-supplied; see the module doc).  `P σ t` is the
    81	flow `P_σ(t)`, `e σ` and `ell σ` are `e_σ` and `ℓ_σ`, `lam σ` is `λ_σ`, `e0`

    83	structure GroundFamily (F : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] where
    84	  /-- The bounded flows `P_σ(t)` on `F` (`E:compact-F-block`). -/
    85	  P : ℝ → ℝ → F →L[ℝ] F
    86	  /-- The growing vectors `e_σ` (`E:compact-F-projection`). -/
    87	  e : ℝ → F
    88	  /-- The growing duals `ℓ_σ` (`E:compact-F-projection`). -/

    90	  /-- The rates `λ_σ = √(-E_1(σ))` (`P:compact-ground-family`). -/

    92	  /-- The data `e_0` (`S:actual-raw-block-lower`, line 15). -/

    94	  /-- The bounded observable `O_φ` (`S:actual-raw-block-lower`, line 15). -/
    95	  obs : F →L[ℝ] ℝ
    96	  /-- The uniform rate gap `d_0` (`E:compact-rate-gap`). -/
    97	  d0 : ℝ
    98	  /-- `λ_σ ≥ √ε > 0` on `I` (`E:compact-rate-gap`; positivity only). -/
    99	  lam_pos : ∀ σ ∈ paramI, 0 < lam σ
   100	  /-- `ℓ_σ(e_σ) = 1` (`E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   101	  ell_e : ∀ σ ∈ paramI, ell σ (e σ) = 1
   102	  /-- `P_σ(t)Π_σ = e^{λ_σ t}Π_σ` (`E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   103	  P_Pi : ∀ σ ∈ paramI, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
   104	    (P σ t).comp ((ell σ).smulRight (e σ)) =
   105	      Real.exp (lam σ * t) • (ell σ).smulRight (e σ)
   106	  /-- `Π_σP_σ(t) = e^{λ_σ t}Π_σ` (`E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   107	  Pi_P : ∀ σ ∈ paramI, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
   108	    ((ell σ).smulRight (e σ)).comp (P σ t) =
   109	      Real.exp (lam σ * t) • (ell σ).smulRight (e σ)
   110	  /-- `d_0 > 0` (`E:compact-rate-gap`). -/
   111	  d0_pos : 0 < d0

   114	  normalized_complement : ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → η < d0 → ∃ C : ℝ,
   115	    ∀ σ ∈ paramI, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
   116	      ‖Real.exp (-(lam σ * t)) •
   117	          (P σ t).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ F - (ell σ).smulRight (e σ))‖

   124	  margin_ell : 0 < ⨅ σ : paramI, ell σ e0

   130	variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (G : GroundFamily F)
   131	
   132	/-- The rank-one projection `Π_σ = e_σ ℓ_σ` (`E:compact-F-projection`). -/
   133	def Pi (σ : ℝ) : F →L[ℝ] F := (G.ell σ).smulRight (G.e σ)
   134	
   135	/-- The complementary projection `Q_σ = I - Π_σ` (`E:compact-F-projection`). -/
   136	def Q (σ : ℝ) : F →L[ℝ] F := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ F - G.Pi σ
   137	
   138	/-- The margin `a_* = inf_I ℓ_σ(e_0)` (TeX line 254). -/
   139	def aStar : ℝ := ⨅ σ : paramI, G.ell σ G.e0
   140	
   141	/-- The margin `j_* = inf_I O_φ(e_σ)` (TeX line 254). -/
   142	def jStar : ℝ := ⨅ σ : paramI, G.obs (G.e σ)
   143	
   144	/-- `Π_σ x = ℓ_σ(x) e_σ` (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   145	theorem Pi_apply (σ : ℝ) (x : F) : G.Pi σ x = G.ell σ x • G.e σ := rfl
   146	
   147	/-- `Q_σ x = x - ℓ_σ(x) e_σ` (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   148	theorem Q_apply (σ : ℝ) (x : F) : G.Q σ x = x - G.ell σ x • G.e σ := rfl
   149	
   150	/-- `ℓ_σ P_σ(t) = e^{λ_σ t} ℓ_σ` (from `E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   151	theorem ell_P {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ∈ paramI) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) (x : F) :
   152	    G.ell σ (G.P σ t x) = Real.exp (G.lam σ * t) * G.ell σ x := by
   153	  have h := congrArg (fun T : F →L[ℝ] F => G.ell σ (T x)) (G.Pi_P σ hσ t ht)
   154	  simpa [ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_apply, G.ell_e σ hσ] using h
   155	
   156	/-- `P_σ(t)e_σ = e^{λ_σ t}e_σ` (from `E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   157	theorem P_e {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ∈ paramI) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
   158	    G.P σ t (G.e σ) = Real.exp (G.lam σ * t) • G.e σ := by
   159	  have h := congrArg (fun T : F →L[ℝ] F => T (G.e σ)) (G.P_Pi σ hσ t ht)
   160	  simpa [ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_apply, G.ell_e σ hσ] using h
   161	
   162	/-- `ℓ_σ Q_σ = 0` (TeX line 280, `ℓ_s(r) = 0`). -/
   163	theorem ell_Q {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ∈ paramI) (x : F) : G.ell σ (G.Q σ x) = 0 := by
   164	  simp [Q_apply, G.ell_e σ hσ]
   165	
   166	/-- `Q_σ² = Q_σ` (TeX line 281, `r = Q_s z`). -/
   167	theorem Q_Q {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ∈ paramI) (x : F) : G.Q σ (G.Q σ x) = G.Q σ x := by
   168	  rw [Q_apply (x := G.Q σ x), G.ell_Q hσ, zero_smul, sub_zero]
   169	
   170	/-- `z = ℓ_σ(z)e_σ + Q_σ z` (TeX line 280, `z = Ae_s + r`). -/
   171	theorem decomp (σ : ℝ) (x : F) : x = G.ell σ x • G.e σ + G.Q σ x := by
   172	  simp [Q_apply]
   173	
   174	/-- `P_σ(t)Q_σ = Q_σP_σ(t)` (from `E:compact-F-eigen`). -/
   175	theorem P_Q {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ∈ paramI) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) (x : F) :
   176	    G.P σ t (G.Q σ x) = G.Q σ (G.P σ t x) := by
   177	  rw [Q_apply, Q_apply, map_sub, map_smul, G.P_e hσ ht, G.ell_P hσ ht, smul_smul,
   178	    mul_comm]
   179	
   180	/-- `‖Q_σ‖ ≤ 1 + ‖Π_σ‖` (TeX line 258, `M_Q = 1 + M_P`). -/
   181	theorem norm_Q_le (σ : ℝ) : ‖G.Q σ‖ ≤ 1 + ‖G.Pi σ‖ :=
   182	  (norm_sub_le _ _).trans (by gcongr; exact ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le)
   183	
   184	/-- `‖Π_σ‖ = ‖ℓ_σ‖‖e_σ‖` (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   185	theorem norm_Pi (σ : ℝ) : ‖G.Pi σ‖ = ‖G.ell σ‖ * ‖G.e σ‖ :=
   186	  ContinuousLinearMap.norm_smulRight_apply _ _
   187	
   188	/-- `‖Π_b - Π_c‖ ≤ ‖e_b‖‖ℓ_b - ℓ_c‖ + ‖ℓ_c‖‖e_b - e_c‖` (auxiliary to the
   189	Lean proof route: continuity of `Π` from that of `e, ℓ`). -/
   190	theorem norm_Pi_sub_le (b c : ℝ) :
   191	    ‖G.Pi b - G.Pi c‖ ≤ ‖G.e b‖ * ‖G.ell b - G.ell c‖ + ‖G.ell c‖ * ‖G.e b - G.e c‖ := by
   192	  refine ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _ (by positivity) (fun x => ?_)
   193	  have hx : (G.Pi b - G.Pi c) x =
   194	      (G.ell b - G.ell c) x • G.e b + G.ell c x • (G.e b - G.e c) := by
   195	    simp only [sub_apply, Pi_apply, sub_smul, smul_sub]
   196	    abel
   197	  rw [hx]
   198	  calc ‖(G.ell b - G.ell c) x • G.e b + G.ell c x • (G.e b - G.e c)‖
   199	      ≤ ‖(G.ell b - G.ell c) x‖ * ‖G.e b‖ + ‖G.ell c x‖ * ‖G.e b - G.e c‖ := by
   200	        refine (norm_add_le _ _).trans ?_
   201	        rw [norm_smul, norm_smul]
   202	    _ ≤ (‖G.ell b - G.ell c‖ * ‖x‖) * ‖G.e b‖ + (‖G.ell c‖ * ‖x‖) * ‖G.e b - G.e c‖ := by
   203	        gcongr
   204	        · exact ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm _ _
   205	        · exact ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm _ _
   206	    _ = _ := by ring
   207	
   208	/-- `e^{λ_σ t} ≥ 1` for `t ≥ 0` (TeX line 297, "since `λ_c > 0`"). -/
   209	theorem exp_ge_one {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ∈ paramI) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
   210	    1 ≤ Real.exp (G.lam σ * t) :=
   211	  Real.one_le_exp (mul_nonneg (G.lam_pos σ hσ).le ht)
   212	
   213	end GroundFamily

   219	def chainState (D : ℕ → ℝ → F →L[ℝ] F) (B : ℝ) (e0 : F) : ℕ → F
   220	  | 0 => e0
   221	  | m + 1 => D m B (chainState D B e0 m)
   222	
   223	/-- Unfolding of `chainState` (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   224	@[simp] theorem chainState_zero (D : ℕ → ℝ → F →L[ℝ] F) (B : ℝ) (e0 : F) :
   225	    chainState D B e0 0 = e0 := rfl

   229	    chainState D B e0 (m + 1) = D m B (chainState D B e0 m) := rfl
